topics.name: Reinforcement learning and agent control
topics.summary: These papers study reinforcement learning and robot or agent control using simulators, rollouts, and delayed-feedback tasks; analyses find that reward design, structured exploration, and self-correction materially change reliability.

topics.name: Medical imaging and clinical AI
topics.summary: These papers study clinical diagnosis and affective health modeling using imaging, physiological signals, and longitudinal cases; analyses find that anatomy-aware features and explicit evaluation improve robustness but reveal transfer limits.

topics.name: Scientific and web agents with memory and tools
topics.summary: These papers study tool-using agents for science, browsing, and design using retrieval, simulation, and multi-step task benchmarks; analyses find that memory, verification, and controllable exploration are central to dependable automation.

topics.name: Persistent and embodied agent systems
topics.summary: These papers study long-lived, embodied, and domain-specific agents using evolving logic, synthetic environments, world-state models, and memory-aware control; analyses find that continuity and context-sensitive recovery are prerequisites for reliable autonomy.

topics.name: Autonomous navigation and robot motion
topics.summary: These papers study aerial, marine, and road-robot navigation using geometric maps, simulation, and safety-constrained trajectories; analyses find that domain-aware training and structured planning improve transfer under partial observation.

topics.name: Medical reconstruction, segmentation, and deployment
topics.summary: These papers study medical reconstruction, segmentation, and model deployment using CT, ultrasound, MRI, fundus, and multimodal clinical data; analyses find that anatomical structure and uncertainty improve useful metrics while calibration gaps persist.

topics.name: Diffusion generation and generative media
topics.summary: These papers study diffusion sampling, guidance, and generative media using image, video, and medical-editing benchmarks; analyses find that adaptive schedules and drift checks improve controllability without guaranteeing semantic safety.

topics.name: 3D geometry, mesh, and neural rendering
topics.summary: These papers study 3D meshes, poses, scenes, and neural rendering using sparse views, geometric reconstruction, and Gaussian representations; analyses find that structural priors improve fidelity when observations are incomplete.

topics.name: Software engineering, code agents, and security
topics.summary: These papers study coding agents, automated repair, and software security using repositories, code-generation prompts, and controlled repair tests; analyses find that tool restrictions, evaluation design, and review shape reliability and diversity.

topics.name: Multimodal representation learning and adaptation
topics.summary: These papers study multimodal alignment and reusable foundation representations using retrieval, sentiment, LiDAR, and recommendation tasks; analyses find that contrastive learning and lightweight transfer help reuse but remain context sensitive.

topics.name: Biomedical modeling and data reliability
topics.summary: These papers study biomedical and physical signal modeling with reliability analysis using ECG, imaging, geotechnical, and structural measurements; analyses find that domain knowledge helps prediction while missing data and population shift remain limiting.

topics.name: LLM alignment, safety, and preference optimization
topics.summary: These papers study language-model alignment, safety, and preference optimization using preference data, adversarial prompts, and demographic tests; analyses find that targeted supervision improves behavior while surface agreement can remain brittle.

topics.name: Optimization, learning theory, and numerical methods
topics.summary: These papers study convergence, Bayesian search, and constrained optimization using proofs, synthetic problems, and numerical benchmarks; analyses find that structure-aware analysis clarifies when methods scale, generalize, or fail.

topics.name: Graph representation and spatial reasoning
topics.summary: These papers study graph representations for spatial and relational reasoning using dynamic walks, scene graphs, and structured prediction tasks; analyses find that message passing improves relational inference but shift can undermine confidence.

topics.name: Persistent agent memory and state
topics.summary: These papers study persistent memory and state management for agents using multi-session benchmarks and versioned state proposals; analyses find that conflict handling and retention policy matter more than storage alone.

topics.name: Human-centered interaction and conversational systems
topics.summary: These papers study user-facing assistants, uncertainty communication, and dialogue using workflow prototypes, user studies, and conversational tasks; analyses find that transparent interaction helps people interpret and act on model outputs.

topics.name: Explainability, evaluation, and social AI
topics.summary: These papers study explanations and user-facing evaluation of intelligent systems using attribution, counterfactual, affective, and social datasets; analyses find that diagnostic value depends on the task, audience, and fidelity of the explanation.

topics.name: Computational biology, chemistry, and causal modeling
topics.summary: These papers study causal, physical, and statistical modeling in biology and chemistry using mediation, materials, protein, and cell-related data; analyses find that structured priors improve sample efficiency while making identifiability assumptions visible.

topics.name: LLM reasoning, retrieval, and structured language
topics.summary: These papers study multi-hop reasoning, parsing, summarization, and instruction following using retrieval corpora, counterfactual tests, and language benchmarks; analyses find that compressed evidence and hierarchical structure improve reasoning beyond fluency.

topics.name: Online learning, distillation, and RL evaluation
topics.summary: These papers study bandits, self-distillation, and verifier-guided reinforcement learning using delayed feedback, repeated sampling, and policy benchmarks; analyses find that offline scores and single-sample gains can misrepresent coverage and exploration.

topics.name: Factuality, calibration, and model trust
topics.summary: These papers study factuality, hallucination, calibration, and belief preservation using retrieval, persuasion, and constrained-reasoning evaluations; analyses find that confidence and correctness diverge often enough to require abstention and stress tests.

topics.name: Graph theory and neural function approximation
topics.summary: These papers study graph structure, ReLU approximation, and network expressivity using formal bounds and small numerical experiments; analyses find that depth and width choices connect approximation quality with generalization.

topics.name: Benchmarks, data quality, and anomaly evaluation
topics.summary: These papers study dataset quality, prompt contamination, and anomaly-evaluation protocols using labeled corpora and controlled scoring audits; analyses find that small changes in data or metrics can reverse conclusions about model quality.

topics.name: Parameter-efficient adaptation and resource-aware tuning
topics.summary: These papers study low-rank, contextual, and resource-aware foundation-model adaptation using multimodal and constrained fine-tuning tasks; analyses find that careful updates deliver useful quality-cost tradeoffs under limited compute.

topics.name: Time-series and sequential forecasting
topics.summary: These papers study sequence forecasting with physical or generative augmentation using future-state prediction and time-series benchmarks; analyses find that multiscale context helps, but domain shift and uncertainty remain central.
